purpose: Frozen exact-example manifest for the T-MIXED finalization-contract probe. Use this instead of regenerating examples from historical salted-hash RNG code.
known_generator_risk: Historical T-MIXED generator scripts used Python hash(domain) in RNG seeds, which is salted by process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed. This manifest freezes the actual evaluated contexts from logged model I/O.

examples.query: studies reporting improvement in clinician burnout levels
examples.context:
[P01] A quality improvement initiative targeting hand hygiene compliance raised adherence rates from 72 to 94 percent across all clinical wards.

[P02] Pandemic-related workload exacerbated the sense of moral distress, as physicians reported feeling unable to provide adequate care despite growing personal sacrifice.

[P03] The post-merger restructuring intensified emotional exhaustion among ward nurses, with compassion fatigue scores increasing from 5.1 to 7.8 over the six-month integration period.

[P04] The hospital's electronic prescribing system was upgraded to version 7.2, improving medication reconciliation compliance from 74 to 91 percent across inpatient wards.

[P05] New antimicrobial prescribing guidelines emphasising culture-directed therapy were adopted by all acute trusts in the region following a collaborative quality-improvement initiative.

[P06] Emotional depletion ratings among community health nurses were substantially attenuated after the introduction of flexible rostering; mean scores fell from 7.2 to 4.3 on the occupational exhaustion inventory.

[P07] A cluster-randomised trial found that moral injury burden was notably abated in wards that adopted collaborative ethical frameworks, with the MIQ score improving by 2.4 points.

[P08] A longitudinal study of intensive care physicians found that the moral distress index was significantly alleviated following the introduction of peer-support circles, with scores declining from 68 to 41 on the validated wellbeing scale.

examples.query: research showing fewer diagnostic errors or improved diagnostic accuracy
examples.context:
[P01] A nationwide survey of pharmacy practice found that medication-dispensing error rates remained stable at 0.9 per 10,000 transactions, with no significant trend over five years.

[P02] The implementation of structured handover checklists curtailed the incidence of missed diagnoses in the emergency department, with diagnostic discordance rates dropping from 8.3 to 2.1 percent over the trial period.

[P03] Procurement of a mobile CT unit enabled stroke imaging in rural ambulances, cutting the median time from symptom onset to treatment by 34 minutes.

[P04] The cardiology department introduced a remote cardiac monitoring programme that enrolled 2,400 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in the first year.

[P05] Delayed diagnoses of sepsis were largely abated after the electronic alert system was calibrated to flag borderline lactate values; door-to-antibiotic time improved by 47 minutes.

[P06] The rate of pathological misclassification was meaningfully attenuated following the adoption of multidisciplinary tumour board reviews, particularly for rare haematological malignancies where concordance improved by 31 percentage points.

[P07] Overdependence on anchoring bias was progressively ameliorated through simulation-based training, and novice residents showed a 26 percent lower frequency of premature diagnostic closure.

[P08] Automation bias intensified as reliance on clinical decision support tools grew, with physicians less likely to override erroneous flagging compared with the pre-implementation era.
